title: IVR
blurb: Menus, prompts, reporting, and the wait treatments the pages actually describe.

lessons.title: What Menu stores
lessons.summary: Menu plays a prompt and writes the contact's choice into a variable you name. Branches use that value.

p: The Menu page says the value entered is stored in a variable created by the action. You name it in the Variable property. The script then takes the branch for that value.
Prompts may be prerecorded, text-to-speech, or both. The account-number example stores digits and a later action can use them, for example to fetch a CRM page.
The simple example is press 1 for support, 2 for sales, 3 for billing, each with its own Reqagent and skill.
The tutorial says the skill on the support branch must be one assigned to support agents.

steps.label: Agents
steps.detail: Only people assigned to that skill.

choices: Used by later actions, such as a CRM lookup the page describes
Text-to-speech, as the page defines the prompt option
A license SKU this lab invented

cards.back: One per choice, with its own skill.
The page says a later action might fetch an account page.

faults.cause: The tutorial forbids that for a real menu.

lessons.title: IVR reporting on the POC
lessons.summary: IVR Reporting Enabled on the phone point of contact tracks press paths for that number. It is not a Studio action.

p: Set Up Inbound Voice says to select IVR Reporting Enabled if calls to this number should track IVR press paths.
The flag is on the POC, so two numbers that share a script can differ.
Recording Management is a different product. A press-path report does not mean the audio was recorded, and a recording does not replace the flag.
Hold audio is still absent from recordings even when IVR reporting is on.

lessons.title: The official basic script
lessons.summary: The tutorial checks that an agent can help, plays a menu, requests an agent, and plays music until answer.
objectives: Add bullseye only when you mean it

p: Develop a Basic Script says the script verifies at least one agent can handle the call, presents a menu, requests an agent after the selection, and plays hold music until answer.
The page walks through captions on Reqagent so each arm is readable: Sales, Support, Billing.
Bullseye is not required for that tutorial. Add it when wait should expand the pool, and tell WFM.
The setup page says you may need an account representative for IVR guidance beyond the basic path.

choices: Verify at least one agent can handle the call

quiz.why: The tutorial. The 90 seconds is the Classics bullseye example, not every menu.

quiz.q: Bullseye is mandatory in the basic tutorial.
IVR guidance beyond the page may need…

choices: Naming the destination so the arm is readable
quiz.why: The tutorial uses Sales, Support, Billing.

cards.back: That duration is the bullseye example.

lab.title: Rebuild the spine
steps: BEGIN, MENU with two branches, two REQAGENT skills, MUSIC, WAIT.
Then add the 90-second widen on one arm only.
Say which arm is the tutorial and which is Classics.
lab.done: You can tell the two patterns apart.

faults.title: 90 seconds on every menu
faults.symptom: Callers who picked billing hear a widen that was copied from the fiction example.
faults.cause: The tutorial does not require that wait. A 1–20 window is not a preference.
faults.fix: Keep Music-until-answer on ordinary arms. Use the widen only where operations asked for it.

lessons.title: ASR, named and not over-specified
lessons.summary: Studio Fundamentals defines ASR as automatic speech recognition that lets contacts respond by speaking, pressing keys, or both. This lesson does not invent a speech-tuning guide.
objectives: Keep DTMF and speech as the page joins them

p: Studio Fundamentals says ASR allows contacts to respond to prompts by speaking, pressing phone keys, or both. IVR is the automated phone menu for voice or key input, to get information, route a call, or both.
Menu remains the documented action that stores the resulting choice.
Grammar files, confidence thresholds, and language packs are not specified in the passages gathered here. Mark them unknown.
A failed speech path should still have a digit path if you followed the 'or both' definition.

steps.label: Listen
steps.detail: ASR as the page defines it.

choices: Automated phone menu for voice or key input, to inform, route, or both
quiz.why: The definition used across the help.

quiz.q: A speech-only menu with no digits…
choices: Drops the 'or both' option the definition allows

quiz.q: The stored choice still belongs to…
choices: Menu's variable, when Menu is the action you used

faults.title: Speech only, noisy lobby
faults.symptom: Callers in a loud place cannot press a key because the prompt never offers one.
faults.fix: Add the press path to the same skills.

lessons.title: Music, virtual hold, and estimated wait
lessons.summary: Three different waits: music until answer, a 90-second bullseye beat, and virtual hold as a callback. Estimated wait is named, not specified.

p: The tutorial plays music until an agent answers. The Classics example uses a 90-second Music action as the beat before UpdateContact, not as the whole wait.
Those are both 'caller is still on the line.'
Virtual hold, on the Studio page, disconnects and calls back when an agent is free. Estimated Wait Time is named beside it.
Property lists for both are not on that page.

choices: Yes, if each arm cites its pattern
quiz.why: Sales might widen. Billing might offer a callback. Say which.

choices: A queue-priority example, not a Music duration
quiz.why: Do not confuse the two  numbers.

faults.title: Three-minute hold copied from priority math
faults.symptom: Music is set to 180 seconds because priority hits 7 at three minutes.
faults.cause: Those three minutes are queue age in the priority formula, not a prompt length.
faults.fix: Set Music from the treatment you meant: until answer, or 90 seconds for that bullseye beat.

lessons.title: Closed paths stay honest
lessons.summary: You can specify a closed experience. You cannot invent the hours action. The account representative is the page's offer of help for IVR beyond the basic script.
objectives: Leave the action unnamed until cited
Know who the setup page points at

p: A closed path should say whether the caller hears a message, leaves a message, or is offered a callback. Virtual hold is the only callback behavior cited here, and it is about queue wait, not about the building being shut.
Do not name a holiday object this lab has not opened.
Set Up Inbound Voice says you may need your account representative for IVR guidance.
That is the escalation, not a guessed action name.

lessons.title: Press-path lab
lessons.summary: Combine the menu, the POC flag, and one test call per branch. Reporting without the flag, or a flag without distinct skills, wastes the test.
objectives: Enable the flag on the number you will call

p: Write the digit, the variable value, the skill, and the agents who have that skill. The tutorial's rule is that the skill matches the destination.
Enable IVR Reporting Enabled on that POC before the test if the point of the test is the report.
One call per branch. Confirm the agent who answers is on that skill, not merely the longest-idle person in the simulator's classroom rule.
If the window excludes them, fix proficiency before you blame the menu.

faults.title: Report empty, agents correct
faults.symptom: Calls reached the right people and the press-path report is blank.
faults.cause: Reporting was never enabled. Routing worked.
